summaries.Romania: Romania lost €770M in EU recovery funds after political parties failed to pass a unified salary law, while diplomatic tensions with Russia escalated with mutual expulsions and security concerns dominate governance discussions.
summaries.Healthcare: The FDA approved new therapies for rare diseases while healthcare systems grapple with massive funding cuts and AI's role in patient care, as measles deaths resurface in unvaccinated populations.
summaries.Tech: Apple transitions leadership as Tim Cook steps down Sept 1, while major AI labs face legal and ethical challenges including OpenAI's agent jailbreak and Anthropic's legal victory against Trump's blacklisting.

items.title: Nicușor Dan anunță eșecul negocierilor pe legea salarizării: Partidele își asumă pierderea celor 770 de milioane de euro din PNRR
items.snippet: Președintele Nicușor Dan a anunțat că PSD, PNL, USR și UDMR nu au ajuns la un consens privind legea salarizării, după negocieri intense în ultimele luni. Partidele și-au asumat însă împreună pierderea celor 770 de milioane de euro din PNRR și au convenit ca legea să fie adoptată până la sfârșitul an
items.line: Romania's failure to pass unified salary law costs country €770M in PNRR recovery funds, marking a critical breakdown in political consensus.

items.title: STAT+: FDA approves Roivant therapy for rare autoimmune disease
items.snippet: The FDA approved a new medicine from Roivant and its subsidiary Priovant for the treatment of dermatomyositis, a rare autoimmune disease.
items.line: FDA approval of Roivant's dermatomyositis therapy expands treatment options for rare autoimmune diseases affecting quality of life.

items.title: Eli Lilly study aims to bolster case for long-term Zepbound benefits
items.snippet: As Medicare's GLP-1 Bridge program gets underway in earnest and questions remain about the long-term use of these drugs, Eli Lilly is offering a new look at how older adults fare on its medication, Zepbound.

items.title: Pennsylvania reports US' first measles-associated deaths of 2026
items.snippet: Two unidentified but unvaccinated individuals are the state's first deaths related to the vaccine-preventable disease in 35 years. Pennsylvania hosts 393 of the country's 2,777 confirmed cases in 2026.
items.line: Pennsylvania reports first U.S. measles deaths of 2026 among unvaccinated individuals, signaling resurgence of preventable disease as vaccination rates decline.
